## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

Three independent bearers, none deriving from another — each is the
only place that reads its payload and each needs its own guard:

- `ProfileSyncListenerService.onMessageReceived` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sync/ProfileSyncListenerService.kt
- `RecordedRaceListenerService.onMessageReceived` — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/sync/RecordedRaceListenerService.kt
- `RecordedRaceAckListenerService.onMessageReceived` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sync/RecordedRaceAckListenerService.kt

## Trigger

`onMessageReceived(event: MessageEvent)`, called by Play Services on
the binder thread when the paired device sends a message on the
service's registered path — observed (already the call site in all
three classes; the gap is what happens once inside it).

## Today

All three classes call `WearableListenerService.onMessageReceived`
directly and read `event.data` with nothing guarding the call:

- `ProfileSyncListenerService` calls
  `PayloadCodec.decodeProfileSync(event.data)`, which runs
  `ObjectInputStream(...).readObject()` on the bytes
  (core-sync/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/sync/transport/PayloadCodec.kt).
  Malformed or truncated bytes make `readObject()` throw
  (`StreamCorruptedException`, `ClassCastException`, and the like);
  nothing on the call site or inside `PayloadCodec` catches it.
- `RecordedRaceListenerService` calls
  `PayloadCodec.decodeRecordedRace(event.data)`, the same
  `ObjectInputStream` path, with the same absence of a guard.
- `RecordedRaceAckListenerService` reads the acknowledged race id with
  `ByteBuffer.wrap(event.data).long`, which throws
  `BufferUnderflowException` on anything shorter than eight bytes;
  nothing on the call site catches it either.

`WearableListenerService.onMessageReceived` runs on the binder thread
Play Services delivers on. An uncaught exception there propagates out
of the binder call and crashes the receiving process — the watch
process for the two `app-wear` services, the phone process for
`RecordedRaceListenerService` — regardless of which device sent the
malformed payload.

## Expected

Each of the three `onMessageReceived` overrides catches the failure of
its own read (`PayloadCodec.decodeProfileSync`,
`PayloadCodec.decodeRecordedRace`, or the `ByteBuffer` read), drops the
payload without acting on it, and reports the failure — per
TECHNICAL_CONVENTIONS.md §13, "never swallow an exception silently:
log it, surface it, or let it propagate" — without letting the
exception escape `onMessageReceived` and reach the binder thread.
Because the three bearers are independent classes in two different
application modules (`:app-wear`, `:app-phone`) with no shared parent
in `:core-sync`, the guard is added at each of the three call sites
separately; none of the three fixes follows from another.
